summary:
I've built the public version at /Users/peterphua/Claude Code/hormone-explainers-public and committed it locally as 61f986b on `main` (61 files, new history, author Peter Phua). I haven't created the GitHub repo or pushed. The internal version at /Users/peterphua/Claude Code/hormone-explainers is unchanged and its git status is clean. The planned live URL is https://optimal-research-team.github.io/hormone-explainers-public/.

**Checks.** I served it locally and ran a Puppeteer sweep of the landing page and all 8 chapters at 1440 and 390, plus reduced-motion and no-WebGL runs. The final runs showed no issues: the WebGL sky and its fallback work, every story step activates, the glossary tooltips open, the chapter menu opens and closes, the contents jumps land on the right step, and there are no console errors, overflow or broken images. Present mode and the exam-room section never show. Some earlier full runs failed on step timing because another session's Chrome was maxing the machine; the same chapters passed in isolation and in a later full run. I looked at the screenshots: 76 are in /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-peterphua-Claude-Code/e8dc4dbd-74ff-4f8f-8adb-ce5c3001a5c0/scratchpad/hxp/shots/qa/ (1440-* and 390-*). The review screenshots show one bug, which I fixed and which also exists in the internal version: chapter 03's contents list read "1Cortisol awakening response" because the step badge digit leaked into the title.

**What changed besides the medical content:**
- **Switched off, not deleted.** Present mode and the "For the exam room" section are behind two flags at the top of `assets/js/site.js` (`presentMode`, `examRoom`, both off). Clinic-only wording is now general.
- **Top bar.** I built it into the existing nav rather than stacking a second bar. It has the wordmark, "The Optimal Menopause Protocol" link and a "Book an intro" pill that opens in a new tab. On phones the protocol link moves into the Chapters menu.
- **Notice and clinic details.** "General education, not medical advice" appears in the landing hero, in a new "About this series" section and in every footer, which also carries the clinic address, phone and email.
- **SEO.** Every page has its own title, description, canonical link, social tags and structured data (MedicalWebPage, audience Patient). These come from `tools/seo-head.py`, which also writes `sitemap.xml` and `robots.txt`. `SITE_URL` and the 404 base href point at the new path.
- **Social cards.** I regenerated all 9 because the old chapter-02 card showed the old title and "Exhaustion".
- **Docs.** `README.md` is rewritten for the public version and points to the internal one. `CHANGES-MEDICAL.md` lists every edit with its reason and source.

**Things to know:**
- **Not clinician-reviewed.** I checked the claims against published sources only. Have a clinician sign off before promoting it.
- **robots.txt won't be read.** On a GitHub Pages project site crawlers only read it at the domain root, so submit `sitemap.xml` in Search Console instead.
- **Hidden text is still in the source.** The switched-off buttons and section are still in the HTML, so crawlers can see text like "Present in the exam room".
- **Old slug.** The chapter 02 page is still named `02-hpa-dysfunction.html`.
- **Not in this task.** The request about improving the "moving line" symptom visualization wasn't part of what I was given here, so I didn't touch it.
medicalChanges: Ch02 reframed from 'How HPA dysfunction evolves' (Normal → Acute → Chronic → Exhaustion) to 'How chronic stress can change the cortisol curve'. Its four curves are now 'patterns seen in research' (Typical rhythm, Short-term stress, Longer-term stress, Flattened rhythm), with the caption 'Patterns seen in research, not fixed stages' (Adam et al., Psychoneuroendocrinology 2017).

Ch02: I removed 'Exhaustion' and 'HPA reactivity fails' as a clinical stage and added: 'Adrenal fatigue isn't a recognized medical diagnosis (Endocrine Society).' The cover caption 'Gradual depletion' became 'A rhythm under strain', and a new line says a flat curve doesn't mean the adrenals have 'run out' (Cadegiani and Kater 2016).

Ch02: I redrew the curves to match research. Short-term stress runs higher but still falls; longer-term stress has a smaller morning rise and a higher evening level; the flattened rhythm is low and flat. I also added the 30–45 minute awakening-rise timing.

Ch02: the AVP sentence is softened to: animal studies suggest AVP takes a bigger part in driving ACTH under repeated stress, and how far this applies in people is unclear (Aguilera 2000). Hypocortisolism in PTSD and chronic fatigue syndrome is noted as mixed evidence (Fries 2005).

Ch03: CAR, slope and AUC are now described as research measures, and the lede no longer says a single value 'says little'. A new step, 'Research measures, not a diagnosis', says salivary curves vary with sleep, sample timing and collection (a first sample 15 minutes late can miss the rise). They aren't validated to diagnose stress-related conditions, and a clinician uses them, if at all, alongside history and other tests. A callout says real disorders are diagnosed with specific blood, urine or late-night saliva tests (Stalder 2016; Endocrine Society guidelines 2008 and 2016).

Ch03: the 'healthy/concerning' verdicts are now neutral: Typical/Flatter, 'Smaller rise · blunted', 'Little drop · flatter', 'Higher or lower total'. The CAR 'shows how well the HPA axis can mobilise energy' became a stated hypothesis.
Ch06: removed alprazolam and benzodiazepines entirely. They aren't appropriate for mood, fatigue or cognition and carry dependence risk (FDA 2020 boxed warning; CANMAT 2023).
Ch06: removed DHEA as a cortisol tool, since there's no good evidence (Nair 2006 NEJM; Endocrine Society 2014). Removed the brand name 'Dayvigo' so only generic names remain.

Ch06: options at each stop are grouped as Foundations, 'Prescription: discuss with a clinician' and 'Limited evidence', with a key on step 1. Ashwagandha, rhodiola, glycine, tryptophan, omega-3, magnesium/B6, B6/folate/magnesium and creatine are labelled limited evidence, and the creatine 5 g/day dose is removed. A note says ashwagandha has been linked to rare liver injury (LiverTox; Björnsson 2020).

Ch06: kept the correctly indicated prescription examples, each marked 'Prescription: discuss with a clinician': daridorexant, lemborexant and low-dose doxepin for insomnia; metformin and GLP-1 medicines for insulin resistance; an SSRI such as escitalopram for mood. Progesterone for sleep is marked limited evidence, prescription.
Ch06: added first-line options: CBT for insomnia (ACP 2016; AASM 2021) and talk therapy. At the mood stop I added the 9-8-8 crisis line.

Ch06: the estrogen stop said only 'Progesterone', which isn't a treatment for low estrogen. It now names menopausal hormone therapy as the most effective treatment for hot flashes and night sweats, with progesterone if you have a uterus (NAMS 2022; SOGC 422a).

Ch06: the melatonin stop now leads with morning daylight, dim evening light and a cool, dark bedroom. The last step keeps 'Medication names are for discussion with your provider, not a recommendation.' and adds that supplements can interact with medicines.

Ch08: 'Mindfulness and connection lift oxytocin, which repairs the HPA axis' became 'Mindfulness practice and social connection can reduce perceived stress and support better sleep' (Khoury 2015; Rusch 2019; Cohen and Wills 1985).

Ch08: '(under 33 dB)' became 'WHO guidance suggests keeping background noise to about 30 dB' (WHO 1999). The 16–19 °C bedroom is kept as 'around 16–19 °C'. 'REM sleep ties to…' became 'Good sleep ties to…'. 'Rebuilding the cortisol curve needs…' now says morning daylight and dim evenings anchor the body clock that sets the rhythm.

Ch08: GLP-1 and metformin are marked prescription, after food and activity. 'Erratic eating and prolonged fasting can worsen HPA dysfunction' became 'long fasts can raise cortisol' (Bergendahl 1996). The supplements layer 'Effective only on top of everything below' became 'Most useful, if at all…; evidence for many supplements is limited, and some interact with medicines'. The line 'the top layer cures all' is removed.

Ch05: framed explicitly as a metaphor in the lede, step 1 and the figure label. 'Stabilise cortisol and thyroid first' became 'Look after the roots, too…', with a callout that thyroid conditions need diagnosis and treatment by a clinician, usually starting with a TSH test. I added that canopy symptoms don't have to wait (menopause symptoms can be treated directly), and removed 'first to suffer… last to recover'.

Ch01: '↑ K⁺' is now tied to aldosterone deficiency (Addison's disease), since cortisol deficiency alone doesn't raise potassium. The deficiency and excess steps now name adrenal insufficiency and Cushing's syndrome (most often from steroid medicines) and how each is diagnosed (Bornstein 2016; Nieman 2008). I added dizziness on standing, weakness, poor sleep and high blood pressure, replaced 'anorexia' with 'loss of appetite', and added that everyday stress moves cortisol within the middle band.

Ch04: oxytocin is hedged as clear in animals but mixed in humans (Cardoso 2014). ANP now says 'in studies', and beta-endorphin is described as the body's own opioid. 'Buffered' became 'offset', with the DHEA and testosterone anabolic balance explained. The see-saw is now 'rhythms run in opposite directions' and no longer says evening cortisol 'keeps melatonin down'. 'Potentially therapeutic' became 'Under study', with 'CBD · early evidence', 'THC · can raise cortisol' and a callout that none of these is an established treatment for stress or cortisol.

Ch07: all twelve connections were corrected or hedged:
- Sleep ↔ melatonin: light suppresses melatonin, and deep sleep (not mainly REM) declines with age.
- Sleep ↔ cortisol: insomnia raises evening cortisol. The claim 'a flat curve is a marker of insomnia' is removed.
- Melatonin ↔ cortisol: the rhythms run opposite, replacing 'high cortisol means low melatonin'.
- Sleep ↔ insulin: the link now runs via obstructive sleep apnea, replacing 'delays sleep onset'.
- Insulin ↔ cortisol: cortisol drives insulin resistance, and insulin stimulating the HPA axis is limited evidence. 'Disables the off switch' is removed.
- PCOS: insulin acts on the ovaries alongside LH, replacing 'raises GnRH'.
- Estrogen from fat: added that fat is the main source of estrogen after menopause.
- Testosterone ↔ cortisol: noted as mostly animal evidence.
- Cortisol → progesterone: the allopregnanolone link is hedged.
- Estrogen ↔ cortisol: oral estrogen raises the protein that carries cortisol, so total cortisol reads higher on blood tests. The CRH and feedback claims are marked as animal data.
- Brain changes: now 'linked to', with the note that some reverse once cortisol normalizes.
- Also added a prompt to see a clinician about ongoing insomnia or loud snoring, and 'start with sleep' became 'Sleep is a good place to start'.

Glossary (assets/js/glossary.js):
- GLP-1 now defines the gut hormone, with GLP-1 medicines mimicking it. The old entry wrongly called GLP-1 a class of medicines.
- Metformin now includes its main mechanism (it lowers the sugar the liver releases) and that it's prescription.
- Aromatase converts androgens, not only testosterone.
- Refined DHEA, DHEA-S, ANP, AVP, oxytocin, catabolism and osteoporosis.
- Added 14 terms the new copy uses: deep sleep, adrenal insufficiency, Addison's disease, aldosterone, Cushing's syndrome, meta-analysis, PTSD, chronic fatigue syndrome, TSH, PCOS, obstructive sleep apnea, progestogen, hormone therapy and perimenopause.

Landing page and footer:
- The night hero caption now says cortisol bottoms out around midnight and then climbs before dawn. The morning caption says melatonin 'fades away' instead of 'stays switched off'.
- The 'General education, not medical advice' notice is on the landing page and in every footer.
- Chapter 07's footer now says the lines show relationships reported in research, not how strong they are.
